commit 8093beca34583c47fba3d66db8094563c267d6db
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 18:22:13 2026 +0530

    twinrx: stop reporting success for checks that did not run
    
    An audit for silent fallbacks. The pattern throughout was the same: a call
    wrapped in except/pass, then carrying on as though it had worked.
    
    _Lifecycle.stop() swallowed a failed stop_hopping() and returned success. That
    is the failure that matters most here -- a hop thread still running through
    teardown keeps issuing timed commands at a device being destroyed, which is
    what leaves the X310's control plane wedged. It now prints the error and says
    a power cycle may be needed.
    
    set_gain() fell back to setting the gain unclamped when the range query
    failed, silently. The gain then may not be the one asked for, and phase moves
    with gain on this hardware, so a calibration measured at the nominal gain
    would no longer apply. Said once, with that consequence spelled out.
    
    Clearing the LO export was silent in twinrx_usrp_source while the hopping
    subclass already reported it. LO routing decides whether channels 2 and 3
    receive anything at all, so a silent failure there reads as two dead channels
    much later.
    
    The LO fallback's retry loop had four silent passes. Only the final outcome
    was printed, so a run could report the fallback failing without any hint of
    which step failed.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit a42d340e2d5d3372080c7b9aa2ad377dcfae948e
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 16:20:21 2026 +0530

    phase_correct_hopping: per-band phase correction for a hopping receiver
    
    phase_correct_hier corrects one set of offsets, read from its file once in
    __init__. That is right for a receiver parked on one frequency and wrong for
    one that hops, because the inter-channel offset belongs to the band. Measured
    on this unit:
    
      pair       2.4 GHz    5.8 GHz    error if the 2.4 table is used at 5.8
      ch1-ch0    +158.4     +67.9                      90 deg
      ch2-ch0     -89.2    +144.1                     127 deg
      ch3-ch0    -175.4    +155.3                      29 deg
    
    Corrections that wrong are worse than none, because the readout still looks
    corrected.
    
    So this holds a row per band and switches rows with the band. It does the same
    arithmetic as phase_correct_hier -- channel 0 straight through, channel N
    multiplied by exp(-j*offset) -- so the two agree on any single band, and
    phase_correct_hier is not touched.
    
    Offsets are entered in DEGREES, which is what the readouts show, and are the
    measured angle_chN - angle_ch0 rather than a correction to apply; the block
    negates them, so a correct table drives the residuals to zero. A file may be
    given instead, in radians, in the format twinrx_hop_test.py --cal-out already
    writes.
    
    The band normally comes from the radio via set_band_freq(), which cannot drift
    out of step with it. An internal dwell schedule is available for standalone
    use and is not the default: two clocks beside one radio eventually disagree,
    and a correction applied to the wrong band reads as a clean, stable, wrong
    phase.
    
    A frequency with no row gets no correction and says so, rather than silently
    reusing the nearest row.
    
    The file reader deliberately does not copy phase_correct_hier's, which runs
    the parsed values through filter(): 0.0 is falsy, so an offset of exactly zero
    disappears and the row comes back one short. In phase_correct_hier that then
    fails the length check and calls sys.exit(1), taking the whole flowgraph with
    it -- feeding it the existing twinrx_session_zero.cfg, three lines of 0.0,
    would do exactly that.
    
    Verified on the hardware's toolchain: degrees converted, a 158.4 deg offset
    rotated to -0.00, nothing applied until a band is selected, unknown band
    refused, file loading, the 2-channel case, and GRC loads the definition.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit edb59e37cfe143de495c02421d3f9fa6eb27d659
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 13:54:23 2026 +0530

    twinrx: keep the DDC out of the timed tune -- this is the stall
    
    Root cause of the radio dying after about seventy hops, and of the power
    cycles.
    
    A DDC block subscribes to time/cmd exactly as a radio does
    (ddc_block_ctrl_impl.cpp:93), so set_command_time applies to it too and its
    register writes are queued in the FPGA command FIFO to execute when the
    block's time reaches the stamp. A radio has a timekeeper and its timed
    commands execute and retire. The DDC's time never advances, so every timed
    write to it is queued and never executes, and never retires.
    
    The FIFO holds CMD_FIFO_SIZE / MAX_CMD_PKT_SIZE = 256/3 = 85 commands.
    Initialisation uses about thirteen, each hop strands one more, and at
    eighty-five the block stops answering:
    
      [0/DDC_0] sr_write() failed: Block ctrl (CE_03_Port_60) no response packet
    
    after which every tune fails for the rest of the run.
    
    Measured failure points: 70, 72 and 74 hops over three runs. A count, not a
    time. It did not move when the host's CPU load was halved, when a Qt
    threading bug was fixed, or when the command-time margin went from 10 ms to
    100 ms -- none of which change how many commands are stranded per hop. It is
    also why only DDC_0 ever fails and never a radio, why a fresh process
    inherits the fault, and why only a power cycle clears it: the full FIFO is
    in the FPGA, not in the driver.
    
    The fix is to stamp only the RF frontend. POLICY_NONE on dsp_freq leaves the
    DDC untouched inside the timed window; it is still set, identically on all
    four channels, by the untimed pass that precedes it. Coherence is unaffected
    -- the four channels share one LO, and what the timed pass exists for is
    making the frontends take effect on the same tick.
    
    Unverified: the run that demonstrates this needs a power cycle first. What
    is established is the mechanism, the arithmetic and the 70/72/74
    reproducibility; what is not is that removing the stranded command removes
    the failure.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

 python/twinrx_usrp_source.py | 43 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++----

commit c6db8e21a7aa6387dfcc05c7c78f3c789951c9bc
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 13:26:19 2026 +0530

    twinrx: give the timed tune a 100 ms deadline instead of 10 ms
    
    The timed tune stamped its writes 10 ms ahead. That is a deadline, not a
    delay: the FPGA holds each write in its command FIFO until that time, and a
    write that arrives after its own timestamp is late and is never
    acknowledged.
    
    One missing acknowledgement is fatal, because of how UHD accounts for them.
    ctrl_iface allows CMD_FIFO_SIZE / MAX_CMD_PKT_SIZE = 256/3 = 85 commands in
    flight unacknowledged, then drains one per new command. Past that point a
    single absent acknowledgement starves the drain: the next write blocks for
    the full 10 s timeout and throws
    
      Block ctrl (CE_03_Port_60) no response packet
    
    and every tune on that block fails for the rest of the run. The API offers
    no way to resynchronise, so the process has to be restarted.
    
    The evidence for a per-command accumulation rather than heating or load is
    the repeatability: 72 hops before the first failure in one run, about 70 in
    another. A count, not a time. It also survived halving the host's CPU load
    and fixing a Qt threading bug, which rules out the host-starvation
    explanation tried before this one.
    
    10 ms had to cover a device time round trip plus eight register writes on a
    host that can be descheduled anywhere in between; one overrun in a few
    hundred is enough. 100 ms costs nothing -- it only postpones a retune that
    already sits inside a one second settle window.
    
    Configurable, so the margin can be measured rather than argued about.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 8cd55d9f614a697f225deefde12d0096cc014896
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 12:57:55 2026 +0530

    twinrx_hopping_source: detect a dead stream and restart it
    
    The X310 can stop sending with nothing in the flowgraph noticing: the plot
    goes flat and the phase readouts hold their last value, which reads as a
    measurement rather than as the absence of one. Reproduced at 14m38s into a
    run, and it does not recover by itself.
    
    The signal used is whether the radio is putting packets on the wire, read
    from the kernel's own counter, not the flowgraph's sample count: when a GUI
    sink stalls, back-pressure stops the source too, and restarting the stream
    would then be the wrong answer to the wrong question.
    
    The restart is a real STOP_CONTINUOUS then START_CONTINUOUS. For more than
    one channel the start is timed rather than immediate, because an immediate
    start lets the four channels begin on different samples, and a constant
    sample skew between channels is a constant phase error -- it would come
    back looking healthy and read wrong.
    
    If no interface carries the expected rate the watchdog says so and stays
    off rather than watching a counter that means nothing. stream_is_alive()
    lets the display say which of the two it is showing.
    
    recv_buff_size defaults to 32 MB, which buys about two seconds of slack at
    4 x 1 Msps. That makes the failure rarer, not impossible.
    
    Measured working: 6 stalls in one run, 6 restarts, each on the first
    attempt, stream back at 15.5 MB/s every time.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit d9b6587cc1a1dda34b78883827a89e31b3491735
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 18:49:08 2026 +0530

    twinrx_hopping_source: stop the hop thread from inside the flowgraph teardown
    
    Putting stop_hopping() in a GRC "main after stop" snippet was too late by
    construction -- that snippet runs after tb.stop() has already returned, so
    the thread spent the whole teardown tuning a device being destroyed. That is
    what left the X310's RFNoC control plane wedged after a shutdown, needing a
    power cycle to recover.
    
    A small sync block inside the hier block now carries the shutdown hook. The
    scheduler calls stop() on every block during top_block.stop(), which is the
    only point a hier_block2 gets while the flowgraph is still alive.

commit f85537d52301bfab35910cc7901ecf3ba51feadc
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 18:26:52 2026 +0530

    Undo the LO fallback's spectrum mirroring in the receiver
    
    Where the fallback puts the LO on the side UHD did not plan for, the DDC's
    correction runs the wrong way and the baseband comes out mirrored: a tone
    sent at centre +200 kHz arrived at -200 kHz. That was being worked around at
    the transmitter, by sending that one band an inverted tone -- which made the
    transmitter behave differently per band for a fault that belongs to the
    receiver.
    
    The receiver now mirrors it back, so every band is plainly centre + the same
    baseband offset and the transmitter needs no per-band offsets at all.
    Conjugation cannot be toggled on a conjugate block, so it is done as
    multiply the Q path by -1, whose constant is a runtime callback; the block
    sets it only on bands where its own fallback fired.
    
    Note this negates the measured phase on those bands. It is applied to all
    four channels identically so the measurement stays consistent, but a
    calibration taken before this change is sign-inverted.
    
    Measured: 2.4 GHz +203.8 kHz, 5.8 GHz +209.0 kHz, 5.1 GHz +208.0 kHz -- all
    on the positive side, SNR 71-76 dB.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    twinrx_hopping_source: stop hopping when tuning starts failing
    
    Tuning only fails the way it does here when the device is going away.

    down, and that is what leaves the X310's RFNoC control plane wedged --

    This is the block's own guard. The flowgraph should still call

commit c36fbd30f81dfcbab428e4a3f4dadd20bf3ac0a9
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 18:03:35 2026 +0530

    twinrx_hopping_source: put the transmitter on the first band before tuning to it
    
    The transmitter does not hop on its own -- it sits wherever it was last
    commanded and only moves when the receiver tells it to. But the command was
    only sent from inside the hop loop, not for the initial tune, so the
    receiver opened on band 0 while the transmitter was still parked wherever
    the previous run left it. For the first couple of seconds the two were on
    different frequencies and the band looked empty, until the hop thread's
    first iteration corrected it.
    
    It now commands the transmitter before the opening tune, and starts with
    _settled False so nothing is displayed until the first settle window has
    actually completed. The constructor tunes, but the transmitter and the LO
    both need a moment, and drawing that stretch would be drawing the
    transition as though it were data.

commit d44dbcb6e48caa35cf9b68f90a24d426fdbc2690
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 15:48:48 2026 +0530

    Nothing silent: no synthetic samples, no unrequested reconfiguration
    
    The bench is only worth having if every number on it came from the radio,
    so the quiet paths are gone.
    
    The LO lock fallback is now opt-in and off by default. It rewrote the LO
    whenever UHD picked one the synthesiser would not lock to, which recovered
    5.00-5.14 GHz but inverted the spectrum and re-locked the LO on every
    arrival -- and that is where the 180 degree step on the exporting channel
    comes from. Off, the band reports the failure in full and stays dead, which
    is the truth about this hardware. lo_lock_fallback=True restores it.
    
    dry_run is removed from the hopping block: there is no longer any way for it
    to produce samples without a radio attached.
    
    A band is only declared good when the transmitter acknowledged its retune
    and the LO locked. Otherwise the gate stays shut and it says so, rather than
    drawing whatever happened to be in the buffer.
    
    Swallowed exceptions now report: clearing LO export, reading lo_locked, and
    set_lo_freq all print instead of passing silently. An unknown cpu_format
    raises rather than quietly assuming complex float32.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit fdbfe1e91042f27e45848d633cf6e30682618169
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 15:39:38 2026 +0530

    twinrx_hopping_source: mute the outputs while settling
    
    The settle time only delayed the next hop, so the display kept drawing the
    transition -- half-tuned LO, gain still moving -- as though it were data. A
    gate per channel now holds the outputs at zero from the moment a hop starts
    until the settle window ends, so the plot goes flat while the radio moves
    and only shows samples worth looking at.
    
    It mutes rather than stopping the stream on purpose: a block that stops
    producing would stall the flowgraph through back-pressure. Complex float32
    only, since the other sample formats have nothing to multiply by.
    
    is_settled() exposes the state for anything downstream that wants to ignore
    the blanked stretch rather than average zeros into a result.

commit a66f3e76d4527660b8c79282f851b12a5185d9f4
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 13:13:07 2026 +0530

    Add twinrx_hopping_source: a TwinRX source that hops bands by itself
    
    twinrx_usrp_source is left exactly as it was. The new block subclasses it so
    the radio setup cannot drift apart between the two -- subdev map, antenna
    selection, LO routing and export, the timed double tune and the low-side LO
    lock fallback are all inherited. Only __init__ is replaced, so the stream
    arguments can carry cpu_format/otw_format, which the original hard-codes to
    fc32; the attributes the inherited methods rely on are set explicitly there.
    
    Adds a band schedule: each band carries its own centre frequency, RX gain and
    dwell, with one settling time applied after every switch. In GRC the row for
    each band appears as "Number of Bands" is raised, up to eight. Gain is applied
    before the tune so both settle inside the same window, and lo_locked is
    checked on every hop so a band that stops working is visible rather than
    silent.
    
    A dry_run mode opens no radio, which is how the schedule was verified: with
    0.5 s settle and dwells of 2/1/3 s the measured intervals were 2.51/1.51/3.51 s.
    GRC generation was checked at 1, 5 and 8 bands.
    
    Per-band gain is a calibration hazard worth remembering: inter-channel phase
    offsets shift with RX gain on this hardware, so a phase calibration belongs to
    a (band, gain) pair rather than to a band alone.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 2b01d91ac578294f382719c855a5ae46a54dc5bf
Author: Shankar <jattishankar67@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 21 19:23:39 2026 +0530

    twinrx_usrp_source: default to Rx B as LO exporter, and select the antenna
    
    Two faults on this USRP-2945, both of which made ch2/ch3 look dead.
    
    LO direction.  Upstream hard-codes Rx A as the exporter: ch0 internal +
    export, ch1 companion, ch2/ch3 external.  The A->B MMCX jumpers on this
    unit pass no LO, so ch2/ch3 were left without an oscillator and read
    about 70x down -- indistinguishable from a broken RF path.  Measured
    twice, hours apart: B->A works, A->B does not.
    
    Now defaults to Rx B exporting (external, external, internal+export,
    companion) and takes a lo_export_direction argument, "B" or "A", so the
    upstream arrangement is still reachable.  Exports are cleared on every
    channel first, because UHD refuses a state where two channels export.
    
    Antenna.  Upstream never calls set_antenna, so every channel stayed on
    whatever UHD defaults to.  A TwinRX board has RX1 and RX2, and a channel
    left on the wrong one reads far down.  Now set per channel with the same
    mapping twinrx_lo_check.py uses: A:0->RX1, A:1->RX2, B:0->RX1, B:1->RX2.
    
    Gain and DC-offset calls collapsed into one loop over sources.
    
    Verified on hardware after the change:
    
      readback   ch0 external / ch1 external / ch2 internal+export / ch3 companion
      tone       +50.4  +50.5  +49.9  +50.9 dB
      coherence  PASS, 0.07 deg across retunes
      guru chain ch2/ch3 rose from 1.3e-4 to 1.35e-2
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
